solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Make weak argument about current literature

indicators.note: the argument word goes around the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: a debate is a formal argument
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Someone undermines a case made about modern writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' is the physics symbol I, not 'present-day'; 'about' signals the enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: A direct verb synonym: to sap the strength of someone or something.

clue.text: Pull terrifying woman with amputated leg

indicators.note: a limb is cut off the end, so the leg word is taken away

parts.note: a dragon is a fierce, formidable woman
on is the leg side in cricket

explanation.surface: A frightening woman with a leg missing being dragged.
explanation.walkthrough: The leg side in cricket is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb synonym: to haul something along behind you.

clue.text: College dance is only every now and then

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

indicators.note: alternate letters are taken from the words is only

explanation.surface: A college dance is a rare event.
explanation.walkthrough: Odd letters of IS ONLY give I, O, L.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oxford college, one example of the category.

clue.text: Manoeuvre by ninth earl to acquire island complex

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take in the island letter
to manoeuvre is to move things around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nobleman plots to take over an island in an intricate scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manoeuvre' rearranges BY NINTH EARL, and 'to acquire' adds I among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective meaning intricate and confusing, like a maze.

clue.text: Pond-life stole iPad I lost, carelessly

indicators.note: the remaining letters are jumbled without care
the single letter word is taken away from the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone swiped my tablet near a pond, through my own negligence.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I from STOLE IPAD, and 'carelessly' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Frog larvae are typical small creatures found living in ponds.

clue.text: Start to annoy

definitions.meaning: in golf, to begin a hole by hitting from the tee
an American informal verb meaning to irritate or make angry

explanation.surface: A short instruction to begin irritating someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: begin play in golf, and irritate, informally.

clue.text: Clobber good listener

parts.note: the ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: An instruction to hit a decent listener, or a description of one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clobber' is British slang for clothes or kit, not the verb to hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Clobber is informal British slang for equipment or clothing, the same sense as kit.

clue.text: Eeyore's in trouble; it looks bad

indicators.note: letters in trouble are disturbed, so these are reordered

explanation.surface: Winnie-the-Pooh's gloomy donkey is in a sorry state.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'S of Eeyore's is part of the fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ugly that spoils a view is unsightly, and so looks bad.

clue.text: Finally bother about hugging friend for support

indicators.note: the outer pieces wrap around the friend word
only the closing letter of the word bother is used

parts.note: round can mean about, as in all round
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: Finally pestering someone by hugging a friend for comfort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hugging' wraps the first two pieces around the friend, which slips in after the opening letter; 'Finally' takes the last letter of 'bother'.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb meaning gather to help and back someone in difficulty.

clue.text: Fit bachelor, overcome by beer with foul smell, choked

indicators.note: the bachelor letter is covered over by the beer word, so it sits inside it

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in degrees like BA
BO is body odour
to choke can mean to die, as an engine dies

explanation.surface: A fit young single man, drunk and smelly, choked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'choked' gives DIED, the stall of an engine.
explanation.definitionFit: Physically fit and healthy is the plain meaning of the hyphenated adjective.

clue.text: Secure main lock at first

parts.note: the main is a poetic name for the open sea

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word lock is taken

explanation.surface: Fastening the main lock as the first job of security.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' is the old word for the high sea, not 'principal'.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something fast or watertight, a verb synonym of fasten.

clue.text: King in love with power dealt badly with strong defence

indicators.note: the king letter goes inside the love word

parts.note: amour is French for love, a love affair
R is Rex, king
P is the physics symbol for power

indicators.note: badly signals that the word dealt is jumbled

explanation.surface: A king in love, given power, handles his defences poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts R in AMOUR for ARMOUR; 'badly' makes LATED from DEALT.
explanation.definitionFit: Protected by steel sheeting, as tanks or warships are.

clue.text: Hybrid car with this belt could be erratic

indicators.note: a hybrid is a mixture, here of the letters of car and those of the answer
the mixed letters could be rearranged to spell the word erratic

explanation.surface: A hybrid car with a certain seat belt might behave unpredictably.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer plus CAR, mixed together ('Hybrid'), 'could be' ERRATIC, so ERRATIC minus C, A, R leaves E, R, T, I to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A belt is a band or zone, like a layer or row in a stack.

clue.text: Something given cricket side by the Queen, by right

parts.note: the off side is one half of a cricket field
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
Tories are the right-wing party in Britain

explanation.surface: A cricket team receives a gift from the monarch, by right.
explanation.walkthrough: The off side is the half of a cricket field facing the batsman's bat.
explanation.definitionFit: The collection of money given by a church congregation during a service.

clue.text: Play part in Lear? That's to be reckless

definitions.meaning: the Fool is a character in King Lear, so an actor might take that role

explanation.surface: An actor asks whether taking a role in King Lear is a rash move.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, perform as the Fool; idiomatically, behave foolishly or recklessly.

clue.text: This drains athletics bigwig taking country runs

indicators.note: the bigwig's name takes the country word inside it

parts.note: Seb Coe is an Olympic champion runner who now heads world athletics
land can mean a country
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A sports chief takes over a nation and runs it.
explanation.walkthrough: Seb Coe, Lord Coe, is the British former middle-distance runner now president of World Athletics.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen bowl with holes used for straining away water.

clue.text: Wake up with heavenly body after love? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: read literally this would place the heavenly body behind the love letter
reverses the instruction, so the love letter goes after the heavenly body

parts.note: a comet is a body in the heavens
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Waking to a heavenly body after a night of love, or rather the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' is undone by 'Quite the opposite', so O comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb meaning regain consciousness, much like wake.

clue.text: Far from rare words of praise

definitions.meaning: steak cooked right through is the opposite of rare

explanation.surface: Common compliments, offered generously.
explanation.definitionFit: A steak cooked through; and the phrase used to congratulate.

clue.text: Small bird, fearful, about to come in for seconds

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

indicators.note: one letter takes the place of another in the fearful word

parts.note: shy means timid or fearful
C is circa, about

explanation.surface: A little bird, nervous, allows a change for second helpings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to come in for' replaces the S of SHY with C, making CHY.
explanation.definitionFit: British informal word for tiny, from Little Tich the music-hall comedian.

clue.text: Break profiteer securing backing of record company

indicators.note: the profiteer word holds the reversed letters inside

parts.note: a tout resells tickets at a profit

indicators.note: the record company's name is read backwards

parts.note: EMI is a British record company

explanation.surface: A ticket scalper gets backing from a record label.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing of' turns EMI into IME, which 'securing' puts in TOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A pause or interval in play or activity, a noun synonym of break.

clue.text: Change of heart during victory is to become less convincing

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come in the middle of the victory word

parts.note: a win is a victory

indicators.note: the letters of heart are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A sudden change of heart in the moment of triumph weakens a stance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change of heart' reads as an idiom, but 'Change of' is the anagram signal and 'during' the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Used of an excuse or argument that grows thin or feeble with repetition.

clue.text: Killer wordgame?

definitions.meaning: an executioner who carries out death sentences by the rope
a guessing game where letters are filled in before a gallows drawing is completed

explanation.surface: A murderous puzzle, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: An executioner; and the pencil-and-paper letter-guessing game.

clue.text: Force hospital to be taken over by estate

indicators.note: the hospital letter is absorbed into the estate word

parts.note: a trust is property held for others, an estate
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A hospital is forced to be taken over by a property holding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be taken over by' puts H inside TRUST.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun synonym of force, as a thrust of an engine.

clue.text: Samuel comes back crazy about hard cheese

indicators.note: the word for the setter is read backwards

parts.note: Samuel is the setter, who calls himself me

indicators.note: the crazy word goes around the hard letter

parts.note: mental is slang for crazy
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: The setter returns, mad about a hard cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often call themselves by 'me'. 'hard cheese' looks like one phrase, but 'hard' is the pencil grade H.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swiss holey cheese, an example of the category.

clue.text: 51, separated and single

indicators.note: the two numerals are pulled apart and read separately, so the one is written out as a word

parts.note: 51 in Roman numerals is LI, fifty then one

explanation.surface: A fifty-one-year-old divorcee, now unattached.
explanation.walkthrough: Separate 51 into fifty (Roman L) and one, written as a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Solitary or sole, an adjective synonym of single.

clue.text: Run from charge around lake

indicators.note: the charge word goes around the lake letter

parts.note: a fee is a charge
L is a map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A runner escapes a fine around the lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts L in FEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: run away, escape.

clue.text: Bond's second to infiltrate order — it's blown

indicators.note: the chosen letter slips inside the order's letters, as a spy would

parts.note: the OBE is the Order of the British Empire

indicators.note: the second letter of the word Bond is taken

explanation.surface: A spy infiltrates a British order, and his cover is blown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests 007, but only its second letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodwind instrument, played by blowing through a double reed.

clue.text: Ballesteros, initially 1 up, almost shot under par

indicators.note: shot means ruined or wrecked, so the letters are jumbled
only the opening letter of the golfer's name is used

parts.note: 1 is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Seve Ballesteros, one up, nearly hit a shot under par.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' scrambles B, I, UP and ALMOST together. 'under par' is golf-speak in the surface but means below standard.
explanation.definitionFit: Not functioning at normal level, an idiom for below the best possible.

clue.text: Strip given to Michael Atherton

indicators.note: the letters are found contained within the cricketer's name

explanation.surface: A cricketing captain is handed a strip, perhaps a team shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Atherton was an England cricket captain; 'Strip' suggests a team kit but means a thin piece of wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin narrow strip of wood, as used under plaster.

clue.text: People present telecoms provider with space grade cable when disheartened

parts.note: AT&T is the American telecoms company
an en is a printing space
a dan is a grade in martial arts

indicators.note: the inside letters of cable are removed, keeping only its ends

explanation.surface: A phone company gives customers space, a grade and cable package.
explanation.walkthrough: An en is a typesetting width; a dan is a black-belt grade in judo or karate.
explanation.definitionFit: The number of people who turn up or are there at an event.
